page.layout: One printed page: a list of conclusions in the upper part, a rule, then a heading and a second list in the lower part. Numbers stand in the left margin beside each line. Nothing printed in the margins or below the text. The strip at the right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is left out.

main_text.l: 7, &c. Conclusio Prima. Leges injustæ non obligant Conscientiam, Ea explicatur,
10. Conclusio Secunda. Lex humana potest priori Obligationi superinducere novam obligationem.
12, &c. Conclusio Tertia. Lex à non habente Legitimam Potestatem lata non obligat.
15, &c. Quod fit subditi officium, ubi de facto qui jam non habet imperat, suse disquiritur.
22. Conclusio Quarta. Leges Humanæ per se obligant in generali.
31, &c. Objectioni occurritur, quæ, à Christiani hominis libertate;
36. itemque ei, quæ ab uno Legislatore Deo & Christo ducta est:
37. Ut & reliquis, quæ contra hanc sententiam disputantur.
main_text.head: Sextæ Prælestionis Summarium.
main_text.l: 4, &c. Sub eâ obligatione, quàm Leges inducunt, Conscientia interim libera est.
6, &c. Dubium Primum. De Lege jubente rem Impossibilem.

page.notes: The word after "Secun" at the lower right is cut off by the edge of the page and is not readable. The opening "P" of "Propositio" is a large drop capital, transcribed as one word.
